subject: Hosted API billing cadence and invoicing vs card
messages:
From: Sam Nguyen <sam@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Rate card + billing cadence question for hosted API

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — Acme Health is evaluating Redwood for a set of pilot integrations. I have a couple of quick questions to help our finance team:

- Do you support monthly invoicing (Net 30) for Hosted API usage, or do you require a card on file and charge-as-you-go?
- If invoicing is available, is there a minimum monthly commit or a revenue threshold to qualify?
- Does Redwood accept our PO and remit invoices to payables@acmehealth.com? Any preferred PO format?

We also requested the rate card during the call; could you send the baseline hosted API pricing so we can model costs?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — our procurement cycle is moving fast.

Best,
Sam Nguyen
Product Partnerships
Acme Health
sam@acmehealth.com

--
Attachment: Acme_PO_Template.pdf (stub)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Nguyen <sam@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Rate card + billing cadence question for hosted API

Hi Sam — great to hear the pilot is moving along. Short answers up front, then details below.

- Yes: we offer monthly invoicing (Net 30) for customers above a nominal monthly commit.
- Card on file is supported and often used for fast onboarding; invoicing requires a billing setup and a signed billing addendum.
- We accept POs; we need a PO number and the billing contact. First invoice may require card payment until the credit application is processed.

I attached our Q2 hosted API rate card (Redwood_Hosted_RateCard_Q2_2025.pdf) with baseline list prices for generation, embeddings, and streaming. A few implementation notes that help with modeling:

- Baseline hosted rates (list): generation $0.004/token, embeddings $0.0008/vector, streaming is billed at token rate with a small per-request charge. (See rate card for exact tiers.)
- Monthly invoicing: available for customers with a recurring commit >= $10k/month (committed usage) or via sales approval for strategic pilots.
- Net terms: Net 30 is standard. Net 45 or Net 60 can be considered for enterprise with a 6-month minimum commit and finance sign-off.
- Payment methods: ACH/wire preferred for invoices. We can accept card on file as a fallback.
- PO: please include the PO number on the remittance instructions. We can accommodate your PO template — I attached the one you sent and will pass it to our finance team.

Next steps:
1) If you want invoicing, please confirm the billing contact and PO cadence.
2) If you need Net 45, tell me the expected monthly commit and well route to finance for approval (ccd Sean).

Im ccing Sean (sales lead) to align on discounts/commit structure. Attaching the rate card now.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: Redwood_Hosted_RateCard_Q2_2025.pdf (stub)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Rate card + billing cadence question for hosted API

Marissa / Sean —

Finance chiming in on the terms:

- Net 30 is the default for invoicing. We can onboard Acme Health to monthly invoicing once the credit app is completed and we have their billing contact + remittance instructions.
- First invoice: we prefer to have the first invoice settled (card or wire) prior to enabling invoicing-only billing to ensure PO/payment flow is validated. In practice we often accept card on file for month one and then switch to invoicing from month two onward once the credit checks pass.
- Net 45 / Net 60: available only if Sales secures a minimum 6-month committed spend of >= $50k total and Finance signs off.
- POs: we accept customer POs. Please ensure PO numbers map to the HubSpot deal id; that speeds reconciliation. If Acme wants invoices sent to payables@acmehealth.com, well add that to their account profile.

If you want me to pre-approve a one-time concession (e.g., allow Net 45 for this pilot), tell me the expected volume and rationale, and Ill review.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
From: Sam Nguyen <sam@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Finance Ops <payables@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 15:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Rate card + billing cadence question for hosted API

Marissa / Sean — thanks for the clear rundown. A few confirmations from our side:

- Were happy to start with monthly invoicing (Net 30). Our procurement prefers invoicing rather than card-on-file.
- Acme will provide a PO for the pilot; please send the invoice to payables@acmehealth.com and include PO # AH-2025-177 when you generate the invoice.
- For onboarding: we can process the initial invoice by ACH. If you require card payment for the first invoice while the credit app is processed, we can do that as a fallback.

Could you send the billing addendum / credit application and the invoice instructions for our AP team (billing address, remittance details, Redwood tax ID)? I attached our PO template for your finance team.

Thanks — Sam

Sam Nguyen
Product Partnerships
Acme Health
sam@acmehealth.com

--
